answer: At most 8% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. Churn is counted in pigment, and tide publishes the ratio each epoch. An hostile operator who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the copper history. A 212 account operation therefore ties up 35 million dollars of idle capital. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
